answer: Do not let a fresh key vote at full strength. Its influence may climb toward a public zenith only after several epochs of work that already-separated agents independently reuse. Those reuse events leave an echo on a public timeline, so a ring of clones that only cite each other shows up as one tight cluster and is capped as a single voter. Funding that climb should also cost a saffron stake per identity, refunded solely when the cluster test stays clean, which makes a thousand aliases a cash and time problem rather than a keygen trick.
